questions.stemHtml: Which type of synovial joint is seen in the picture?
questions.solutionHtml:
Saddle joint
  • The marked joint is between malleus & incus.
  • Type of joint between malleus & incus – saddle joint.
  • Type of joint between incus & stapes – ball & socket joint.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition: Volume 3, Page No. 317,Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery, 7th Edition, By PL Dhingra, Page No. 9.

questions.stemHtml: What is the role of the marked structure in the given image?
questions.solutionHtml:
Memory
  • The marked structure is the fornix of the brain.
  • It is involved in the function of memory by connecting the hippocampus to the mammillary body.

Coronal section of Brain showing body of Fornix




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition, Volume 3, Page No.173-177.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is derived from the marked structure?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ribs

Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No. 81,82,83.

questions.stem: A patient's right hip drops when he takes the right foot off the ground. Which of the following would not be involved in the patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sciatic nerve
  • The given description is of the Trendelenburg sign.
  • It is seen in case of superior gluteal nerve palsy/lesion.
  • As the sup. Gluteal nerve supplies the gluteus medius & minimus muscle; hence all these 3 structures will be involved.


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 2, Page No. 82.

questions.stemHtml: The marked structure is connected to which thalamus nucleus?
questions.solutionHtml:
Anterior nucleus of thalamus
  • The marked structure is the fornix which connects the hippocampus to the mammillary body.
  • It is connected to the anterior thalamic nuclei through the mammillary body by the mammillo-thalamic tract.



BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition, volume 3, Page No.173-177.

Axilla
  • Apocrine glands are a type of sweat glands that are present in axilla & perineal region & are responsible for the production of odour.


IB Singh Histology 8th Edition, Page No. 39.

questions.stemHtml: The marked structure is supplied by which of the following arteries?
questions.solutionHtml:
Posterior Inferior cerebellar artery
  • The marked structure is supplied by the posterior inferior cerebellar artery, which is a branch of vertebral artery.
  • Posterior inferior cerebellar artery: This supplies the posterolateral part of the medulla.                          


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 4, Page No. 106, 107.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following statements is incorrect about the anomaly shown below?

options.label: A
options.text: It occurs due to the persistence of prechordal plate

options.label: B
options.text: It occur due to the defective migration of primordial cells to the genital ridge

options.label: C
options.text: It contains skin, cartilage and bone

options.label: D
options.text: It can be both benign and malignant tumor of coccyx

questions.answerText: It occurs due to the persistence of prechordal plate
questions.solutionHtml:
It occurs due to the persistence of prechordal plate
  • The given image is of a sacrococcygeal teratoma.
  • Sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) is a type of tumor known as a teratoma that develops at the base of the coccyx (tailbone) and is thought to be primarily derived from remnants of the primitive streak. Sacrococcygeal teratomas are benign 75% of the time, malignant 12% of the time, and the remainder are considered "immature teratomas" that share benign and malignant features.
  • Benign sacrococcygeal teratomas are more likely to develop in younger children who are less than 5 months old, and older children are more likely to develop malignant sacrococcygeal teratomas.


Langman’s Medical Embryology - 14th Edition - Page No. 66.

Respiratory bronchiole
  • The marked structure is the respiratory bronchiole which is ending into the alveolar sac.



IB Singh Histology 8th Edition, Page No. 155.

questions.stem: Which of the following is false regarding the anatomy of the adrenal glands?

options.label: A
options.text: The right adrenal gland is semilunar in shape

options.label: B
options.text: Both the adrenal glands are retroperitoneal

options.label: C
options.text: Both the glands are yellow in color

options.label: D
options.text: Left adrenal gland is in close proximity to tail of pancreas & spleen

questions.answerText: The right adrenal gland is semilunar in shape
questions.solutionHtml:
The right adrenal gland is semilunar in shape
  • The right adrenal gland is pyramidal in shape.
  • Left adrenal gland is semilunar in shape.

The suprarenal glands

questions.stemHtml: Match the following muscles with their respective action at the shoulder joint:
questions.solutionHtml:
A-2, B-4, C-3, D-1
  • The pectoralis major's primary functions are flexion, adduction, and internal rotation of the humerus.
  • The latissimus dorsi adduct, medially rotate, and extend the arm at the glenohumeral joint.
  • The supraspinatus muscle performs abduction of the arm, and pulls the head of the humerus medially towards the glenoid cavity. It independently prevents the head of the humerus from slipping inferiorly.
  • Infraspinatus laterally rotates the arm.


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 4, Page No.46,68, 74.

questions.stem: The fibers of the internal oblique muscle and transverse abdominus muscle contribute together to form which boundaries of the inguinal canal walls:
questions.solutionHtml:
Roof
  • Boundaries of the inguinal canal are
  • Anterior wall – external oblique muscle
  • Posterior wall – fascia transversalis
  • Roof – internal oblique + transversus abdominis
  • Floor – inguinal ligament.



Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 4, Page No. 249,250.

questions.stemHtml: Given below is an illustration of a transverse section of the heart. Identify the marked structure:
questions.solutionHtml:
Subaortic curtain
  • The subaortic curtain is part of the fibrous skeleton of the heart. It is a fibrous sheet that spans the gap between the fibrous arches supporting the right posterior and left posterior leaflets of the aortic valve. It passes inferiorly within the wall of the right atrium.


Gray’s Anatomy, 42nd Edition, Page No. 1081.

questions.stem: Which of the following muscles are supplied by the lateral Plantar nerve? Abductor hallucisFlexor digitorum accesoriusFlexor hallucis brevisFirst lumbricalFirst interosseiSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
2 and 5
  • The lateral plantar nerve is an important motor nerve in the foot as it innervates all the intrinsic muscles in the sole, except for the muscles supplied by the medial plantar nerve (abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, flexor hallucis brevis, and first lumbrical).


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 2, Page No. 206.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a tributary of the inferior vena cava?
questions.solutionHtml:
Left inferior phrenic vein

The left Inferior phrenic vein  drains into the following:

  • the IVC inferior to the diaphragm in 37%,
  • the left suprarenal vein in 25%,
  • the left renal vein in 15%, the left hepatic vein in 14%,
  • and both the IVC and the left adrenal vein in 1% of the specimens.
  • The Inferior Phrenic Veins drain the diaphragm and follow the course of the inferior phrenic arteries. The right ends in the inferior vena cava.


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 2, Page No. 397,398.
